cells.tense: The pen is in your hand now and you are using it.
cells.ask: In one conversation today, say what you actually notice about the other person before you decide what to do about it. Then let the conversation end.
cells.core: You can be close to someone and still know where you stop. That is not a trick you learned; it is how you are when you are not bracing. You feel what they feel without taking it over, and you stay in your own seat.\n\nWhat you are carrying now is not heaviness. It is the chance to keep going exactly like this. There is something worth holding steady in that. The invitation is not to do more. It is to notice that you are already doing it, and to keep your hand on the pen instead of handing it to whoever is loudest.
cells.sheetLine: You can be close without disappearing into someone else.
cells.place: the open field before anything has chosen yet

cells.tense: You are already spending a future that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick one person you feel pulled to fix today. Do nothing about them. When the urge shows up, write down what you would have said, and leave it there.
cells.core: You feel what other people are feeling before they do. Somewhere ahead is a day where nobody is upset and you are already living in it, so you keep leaning toward it. The leaning is not the problem. It is that you have stopped being able to find the edge of yourself in the middle of it.\n\nThe feeling is real. It is just running ahead of the moment. What you are carrying now is the chance to let one thing stay unfinished. Not coldness, not pulling away, just letting the other person hold their own weight for a day while you stay nearby without taking it on.
cells.sheetLine: You feel people before they ask, and you have lost your own edge.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.ask: At one ordinary moment with another person today — a store counter, a kitchen, a hallway — say one true sentence about what you are feeling right now, even if it is small and awkward.
cells.core: You are not cold. You went quiet to keep going, and the quiet worked. The feeling does not reach you the way it reaches other people; relationships stay on the surface and you let them. That is where you are standing, and it is a real place to stand.\n\nWhat is gone is not the ability. It is the practice. You can still feel with people; you have just stopped letting it in. What you are carrying now is not a feeling to manufacture. It is a small motion back toward the room — one real exchange, one sentence that is yours, and then another tomorrow.
cells.sheetLine: You went quiet to survive, and it worked too well.

cells.tense: The pen is down but the ink is still moving on the page.
cells.ask: Ask one person you trust what they notice about how you treat people. When they answer, do not explain it away. Just say thank you and let it sit.
cells.core: People feel something from you. They come to you when they are low, and they leave lighter, and you would call that nothing. You would say you were just standing there. The connection is real, and it has been running without you signing it.\n\nYou are not indifferent. You are just not at the desk where it gets written. On the good days it runs clean through you: you feel the recognition yourself, the warmth that honors both of you and does not swallow either one. The one thing you could do is not try to feel more. It is to let one person name what you already do, and not correct them. The care is not missing. It is that you keep calling it nothing.
cells.sheetLine: People feel your care. You call it standing there.
